FotoFocusExhibition

Second Look: Danny Ransohoff’s Cityscapes Through New Eyes

56Over-the-Rhine Museum

Details

This exhibition pairs 13 cityscapes taken by Daniel J. (Danny) Ransohoff, an acclaimed mid-20th-century social documentarian who captured evolving views of Cincinnati from the 1950s through the ’70s, with current images of the same locations taken by University of Cincinnati students. By pairing images of the same location taken 50–70 years apart, the exhibition covers not a long distance, but a long span of time. Ransohoff’s photographs were taken during a period of urban decline and shifting neighborhood demographics. His images reveal families, children, storefronts, stoops, and streetscapes that speak to both the resilience and the challenges of the community at that time. In the present day, University of Cincinnati public history undergraduate students revisit Ransohoff’s sites, photographing the same locations from his archive.

By taking a “second look” at these sites, students find a new understanding of Cincinnati’s past and present. Their images reveal what has endured and what has changed, whether through restoration, abandonment, demolition, or new use. Viewed side by side, the paired photographs highlight the seeming permanence of brick and stone alongside the inevitability of change in architecture, culture, and community life. Student-generated text helps fill in the historical narrative. Through these images, curator Anne Delano Steinert and her students remind audiences that cities are living archives. What remains, what disappears, and what emerges all tell stories about the people whose lives and legacies continue to shape Cincinnati across generations.

Artists: Austin Carr, Avery Carter, Connor Herman, Daniel Ransohoff, Matt Enneking

With Anne Delano Steinert (curator)

Cost: Free to the Public

FotoFocusExhibition

Stacy Kranitz: Ain’t No Grave Gonna Hold My Body Down

The Contemporary Dayton

Details

Pulitzer Prize-winning photographer Stacy Kranitz premieres her newest body of work, Ain’t No Grave Gonna Hold My Body Down. Featuring more than 75 photographs drawn from historical archives and Kranitz’s own images, the exhibition demonstrates how Appalachia has been seen and misseen across generations. The result is a complex portrait of a region shaped by myth, exploitation, resilience, and the uneasy tension between representation and reality.

More than 60 years after President Lyndon B. Johnson launched the War on Poverty, Appalachia remains a place where poverty is both deeply entrenched and persistently misrepresented. The initiative was partly shaped by Harry M. Caudill’s 1963 book Night Comes to the Cumberlands, which exposed the exploitation of Appalachian land and labor by coal companies. While Caudill initially framed the “mountaineer” as a victim of industrial greed, he later adopted troubling eugenic ideas, claiming poverty was hereditary and advocating sterilization programs. This shift reveals how the mythology of the mountaineer has evolved, from self-reliant frontiersman to victim blamed for systemic hardship.

Photography has played a key role in shaping these narratives, from early portraits of homesteaders to propaganda, government documentation, and media coverage during the War on Poverty. Over the past decade, Kranitz has built close relationships within Appalachian communities. Her images challenge viewers to confront how photographs can both reveal and distort lived experience, urging a reconsideration of Appalachia and of photography’s power and limits in shaping cultural understanding.

Artists: Stacy Kranitz

With Heather Jones (curator)

Cost: Free to the Public

Source: fotofocus.org (opens in a new tab)

FotoFocusExhibition

The Long Lives We Carry

Clifton Cultural Arts Center

Details

The Long Lives We Carry brings together the work of American photojournalist Gordon Baer (1940–2019) and Slovak photographer Jano Rečo (b. 1948) in a poignant study of aging, care, and the fragile dignity of human life at its end. Baer, a longtime Cincinnati-based photographer, was known for his sensitive documentation of those often overlooked by society. His deeply personal photographs of his dying Aunt Beck and his images from nursing homes in Ohio bear witness to lives frequently hidden from public view. These works capture fleeting gestures of tenderness alongside the stark realities of institutional neglect.

In the early 1980s, Rečo produced Seniors Home as part of a larger photographic cycle examining social welfare institutions in Bohemia. Created through close personal contact with residents, the series moves beyond bureaucratic documentation to expose the emotional complexities of aging in institutional care: community and loneliness, resilience and resignation.

Presented together, Baer and Rečo’s photographs reveal striking parallels across national and political contexts in how societies see, support, and sequester the elderly. Their images invite viewers to consider aging as a universal human condition—one shaped by systems of care, yet profoundly intimate. By placing these works in dialogue, The Long Lives We Carry asks audiences to look closely at lives often pushed to the margins.

Artists: Gordon Baer, Jano Rečo

With Saad Ghosn (curator)

Cost: Free to the Public

FotoFocusExhibition

The Sweep of Time, Beyond the Horizon

Manifest Gallery

Details

A juried exhibition, The Sweep of Time, Beyond the Horizon emphasizes photography’s unique ability to hold two things at once: the instant and what endures beyond it. The horizon, central to the exhibition, functions as both a literal subject and a symbolic threshold—an opening into broader contexts of time, memory, and continuity. In this way, distance and perspective become the focus while also welcoming works that consider temporal scale and duration, creating a space where history and the future coexist. Some works attend to memory and generational connection, while others imagine what lies ahead. Together, they place the present moment within a wider trajectory.

The Sweep of Time, Beyond the Horizon offers a way of seeing that resists the urgency of the immediate. By presenting diverse lens-based works that embody continuity and expanded vision, the exhibition fosters reflection, patience, and a deeper sense of orientation within time.

Artists: Birgit Rudel, Carol Henry, Chuck Miller, Crystal Tursich, Dylan Bannister, Margaret Day, Margo Geddes, Patricia Howard, PJ Sturdevant, Werner Sun

What are the costs and consequences of allegiance? This We Believe explores the power and evolution of belief systems—religious, political, economic—and how adherence to and rejection of these ideologies has influenced our current global culture of divisiveness and polarization. From imagery of disillusionment and protest, to revelations of historical complexity and visions of transcending binary definitions of identity, the artworks featured question and critique unalloyed allegiance to creed or country.

FotoFocusExhibition

Witness to the Journey: Matt Herron and the Deep South, 1965

55National Underground Railroad Freedom Center

Details

Witness to the Journey: Matt Herron and the Deep South, 1965 presents a compelling selection of 28 black-and-white photographs by renowned civil rights photographer Matt Herron. This exhibition documents the historic Selma to Montgomery March for Voting Rights, a pivotal moment in American history that directly led to the passage of the Voting Rights Act of 1965. Herron’s images capture the spirit, struggle, and triumph of the marchers—ordinary citizens, activists, and leaders—who walked 54 miles over five days to demand justice. The photographs reveal the diversity of participants, the role of music and federal protection, and the emotional highs and lows of the journey. The exhibition concludes with images reflecting the immediate impact of the Voting Rights Act and the ongoing fight for voter equity. By revisiting these images in 2026, America’s 250th anniversary, the exhibition encourages reflection on how far we’ve come and how far we still must go.

Presented in the Freedom Center’s Skirball Gallery, the exhibition will be accompanied by Herron’s personal effects, including his leather camera bag and hip carrier, contextualizing the photographs and the broader Civil Rights Movement. Selected images are sourced from an exhibition originally curated by Herron and now part of the Freedom Center’s museum collection, offering a powerful lens into the moral arc of history and the enduring pursuit of justice.

Artists: Matt Herron

Cost: Free to Pass Holders in October, venue members, and children 2 and under. General admission: $19.50 adults; $17.50 seniors; $16.50 children 3–17.

Art on The Rise: Fall Fun

38Cincinnati Art Museum

Free · museum · families · special events

Details

Kick off the afternoon at 1 p.m. with a brief meditation session from our partner, The Well!

Following the meditation, creativity starts to flow as we prepare for the 2 p.m. performance of Ecotone: Sonic Ascent, a community sound art installation designed and produced by J. Howd. Five musical performances will transform five different plazas on the Art Climb into distinct sonic worlds. Inspired by the themes of Cosmic Cafe, Fairyland Forest, Crystal Cathedral, Haunted Shipwreck, and Steampunk Junkyard, the performance will create an evolving soundscape that changes with every step.

There is no single place to experience the performances—and that’s the point—wander, climb, pause, listen, and discover how the music shifts as you move between plazas. A melody heard from one level may blend with a rhythm from another; sounds that seem separate from one location may unexpectedly become part of a larger musical composition from another.

You are invited to join the performance with musical instruments, which you can make at the CAM Cruiser before the music starts, or percussion instruments that will be provided. With your help, we will create an immersive, site-specific musical journey where architecture, movement, imagination, and sound all come together.

From 3–5 p.m. we invite you to create a Community Canvas with Happen Inc., celebrating the fall season. The five plazas will continue to host our thematic visual interpretations, creating a perfect end-of-day photo op for guests.

Agenda:

1 p.m. Five-minute meditation with The Well 1–2 p.m. Instrument making with the CAM Cruiser and collaborative set building 2–3 p.m. PERFORMANCE, Ecotone: Sonic Ascent 3–4 p.m. Community Canvas with Happen Inc. and photo opportunities with sets

Cost: Free. Reservations not required.

Jim Henson’s Fraggle Rock: Back to the Rock LIVE

27Aronoff Center for the Arts · Procter & Gamble Hall

family · puppetry

Details

Gobo, Red, Mokey, Wembley, and Boober Fraggle discover the legend of the Celebration Stone – an ancient Fraggle treasure that has the power to bring everyone together for the greatest party of all time but was shattered and lost generations ago. As the Fraggles set off on an exhilarating, adventurous journey exploring exciting new caves within Fraggle Rock and even beyond, they discover magic that they never knew existed and learn to work together to unite the lost pieces of the magical artifact. Can the Fraggles succeed in their quest to bring the Celebration Stone back to Fraggle Rock so everyone can enjoy the most incredible party in Fraggle history? And, along the way, will they find something even more memorable and heartfelt than they could have ever imagined?

Featuring gorgeous new walk-around versions of the Fraggles; puppet-sized Doozers; an appearance from a giant Gorg; and exclusive, new, wondrous puppet creatures from the acclaimed Jim Henson’s Creature Shop, along with fan-favorite songs and exciting visual effects, this all-new musical stage adventure welcomes audiences on a joyful, nostalgia-filled trip to Fraggle Rock. Filled with music, laughter, and imagination, it’s an unforgettable live experience that will have Silly Creatures of all ages dancing in the aisles!

Written and directed by John Tartaglia (Avenue Q, Shrek the Musical, Stephen Schwartz’s The Secret Silk), this first-ever, live Fraggle show includes fantastic in-theater immersive special effects, audience interactivity, magical heartwarming moments, hilarious and endearing new characters, and much more to make this stage production perfect for families with young first-time theater goers and for Fraggle Rock fans who remain young at heart.

Bring a non-perishable food donation to the Aronoff Center and help fill the van for the Friars Club. Together, we can make a big impact for neighbors in need. Mutual Dance Theatre presents South Chicago Dance Theatre

27Aronoff Center for the Arts · Jarson-Kaplan Theater

KSKia S. Smith

dance

Details

"THE NEXT BIG THING" — Chicago Tribune

The highly buzzed-about South Chicago Dance Theatre makes its Cincinnati debut, presented by Mutual Dance Theatre's Jefferson James Contemporary Dance Theater Series! Led by Artistic Director Kia S. Smith, whose rise has been described as "meteoric," South Chicago Dance Theatre landed a spot on Dance Magazine's national "must-see" list and has been called “the next big thing” by the Chicago Tribune.

Described as a "rare combination of rigor and vulnerability" (Third Cost Review), South Chicago Dance Theatre blends legacy with innovation and is the largest company in Mutual's 26-27 season.

This program includes a short excerpt from Smith's Josephine Project, which traces her great-grandmother's journey north out of the Jim Crow South, documented by hand-written notes in a preserved suitcase used during the Great Migration.

The Josephine Project is only one of five works in the concert. The presentation features another of Smith's choreographies called Suite on the Sahara, as well as works by a multi-cultural slate of guest choreographers: On a Lark by Stephanie Martinez, Slip Force by Natasha Adorlee, and Subject(s) Verb Object! by David Dorfman.

For more information, visit mutualdance.org/southchicago.

MorePerformance

Holly Bowling

52Memorial Hall

HBHolly Bowling

concert · piano

Details

Cast aside any and all expectations.

Whether behind the piano on a windswept mountainous cliff, at a hallowed venue such as Carnegie Hall, or playing shoulder-to-shoulder with some of the most legendary musicians in history, solo pianist Holly Bowling subverts convention with virtuosic playing, emotional immersion, and a thirst for invention. Acclaimed by Rolling Stone, Billboard, Relix, and more and sought-after by icons such as Phil Lesh, Bob Weir, and Warren Haynes, she once again flips the script on her 2020 album and second reimagining of Grateful Dead staples entitled Seeking All That’s Still Unsung.

“When you go to see someone play solo piano, you’re not expecting them to stand up, pluck the strings, drum on the frame, hit the strings with mallets, or place magnets and EBows inside of the piano,” she smiles. “It doesn’t fit with the expectations of how you’re supposed to play this instrument. I think it works though.”

Cost: $30.00 - $44.00 inc. $4 service charge

Pound for pound, Brad Williams is the funniest comedian in the country right now and has become one of the most in-demand comedians working today. Williams started doing stand-up comedy as a teenager and has been touring successfully ever since, routinely selling out prestigious venues all over the country and world.

Williams has parlayed his live performances into a multitude of stand-up television appearances, including The Tonight Show, Dave Attell’s Comedy Underground, and Jimmy Kimmel Live. His first one-hour special, Fun Size, was the highest rated special on Showtime, and a year later, he followed that up with his second one, Daddy Issues, which was even more successful than the first. His third special in three years was an uproarious one, hosting some of the edgiest comedians in the country from the prestigious Montreal Just for Laughs Festival. StartupCincyPanel

The Factory Floor Robotics Evolution

Location not listed

Antony Seppi, jeremy jarrett and 2 more

HardTech

Details

Robotic arms have been the backbone of manufacturing for decades, but deploying them in modern, agile factory environments still presents massive integration, software, and safety challenges. At the same time, the hardware world is flooded with hype surrounding humanoid robots, leaving many to wonder if traditional articulated arms are on the verge of extinction. This session cuts through the noise to examine the true state of manufacturing robotics. We will break down the immediate technical hurdles of deploying next-generation arms, explore new sensing and AI technologies keeping them relevant, and debate whether the future belongs to specialized, highly efficient arms or flexible, human-shaped machines.

Resilience Requires Creativity: Why the Organizations Built to Survive Uncertainty Aren't Necessarily the Ones Built for Efficiency

Location not listed

Chris Ritter, Christopher A. Ritter Art Direction, Branding & Design

Founder Journey

Details

Today's businesses face volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity at a scale few organizations were designed to handle. Yet when uncertainty rises, our instinct is often to seek more control: optimize processes, reduce risk, eliminate waste, and make outcomes increasingly predictable. That instinct may be making organizations more fragile.

Drawing from ongoing graduate research at Parsons School of Design, two decades of creative leadership, and conversations with leaders across design, innovation, and business, Christopher A. Ritter explores creativity as more than a source of ideas. It is an organizational capacity for adaptation.

This talk examines why resilient organizations protect curiosity, experimentation, candor, judgment, and the freedom to explore what isn't yet known—and why the ability to create may ultimately matter more than the ability to predict.

StartupCincyPanel

Growing Our Region Through Bold Bets

Location not listed

Brendon Cull and Abby Grimm

City Building

Details

What happens when a region stops thinking organization by organization—and starts making bigger bets together? Cincinnati’s next chapter of growth will require more than any one company, institution, or initiative. It will take a connected region willing to align around ambitious ideas, combine our strengths, and take bold swings on what’s possible.

To close out StartupCincy Week, regional leaders come together for a forward-looking conversation about the big bets being placed across Cincinnati—from economic development and talent to tourism, placemaking, entrepreneurship, and innovation. We’ll explore where momentum is building, where greater collaboration can unlock new opportunities, and how a more connected region creates the conditions for founders, innovators, and growing companies to thrive. Because when Cincinnati bets boldly on itself, we give the people building what’s next even more reason to build it here.

MorePerformance

Nina Simone Piano Competition

54Cincinnati Music Hall

EHJMJMEvan Hines, John Paul McGee and 2 more

music · classical

Details

The future of the piano takes the stage. Art of the Piano, led by Awadagin Pratt, proudly presents the Nina Simone Piano Competition Finals, an extraordinary evening celebrating the artistry, promise and voices of talented young African American pianists.

Named in honor of the legendary Nina Simone — an artist whose extraordinary musicianship transcended genres and challenged the boundaries of classical music — the Competition provides a highly visible platform for emerging artists to share their gifts, gain professional experience and open doors to new opportunities.

The Competition finals will take place alongside the Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra and through their performances, they represent not only the future of the piano, but the expanding possibilities of who gets to shape the future of classical music. Join us for a breathtaking evening of music and discovery as the next generation takes its place on stage.

All seats are just $35 and include access to the 6 PM Solo Round and the 7:30 PM Concerto Round

Program: Alexander Scriabin Piano Concerto in F-sharp Minor (Hines); Florence Price Piano Concerto in D Minor in One Movement (McGee); Sergei Rachmaninoff Piano Concerto No. 3 in D Minor (Mhoon)

Organizers: Awadagin Pratt

Also with Joshua Mhoon (performer), Cristian Măcelaru (performer)

Cost: All seats are just $35

BLINKExhibition

Harper Alive at The Mercantile Immersive

23The Mercantile Immersive

blink around town · immersive · ticketed

Details

Created exclusively for Mercantile Immersive, Harper Alive transforms the Harpers’ iconic artwork into a breathtaking 360-degree journey of movement, light, music, and storytelling. Wander through vibrant forests, soar alongside birds, encounter playful wildlife, and explore bold geometric landscapes as their celebrated “minimal realism” comes alive all around you.

Your experience begins in the Oculus Gallery, where historical photographs, archival footage, and personal stories reveal the remarkable lives and artistic partnership of Charley and Edie Harper. Then, step into the Vista Room, where floor-to-ceiling LED displays, spatial audio, dynamic lighting, and an original musical score surround you in an unforgettable six-minute immersive experience.

Whether you’re a lifelong Harper admirer or discovering their work for the first time, Harper Alive offers a completely new way to experience two of Cincinnati’s most beloved artists.

MoreParty

People of the Good River Opening Reception

42Contemporary Arts Center

LHLeonard Harmon

museum

Details

Join us as we celebrate the opening, on October 9th, of Lenny Harmon's exhibition, People of the Good River. This show showcases Indigenous culture outside of the outdated stereotypes of history books. People of the Good River challenges these misconceptions by capturing vibrant, everyday realities of Indigenous people living in Cincinnati Today. Grounded by the legacy of the Ohi-yo- the Seneca word for Good River-- this exhibition pairs candid portrait photography with hand-pulled screen printing on paper. Each physical layer of ink builds a portrait of modern life, work, and community, moving past romanticized tropes to celebrate an enduring present and archive the people who are actively shaping Cincinnati's contemporary narrative.

The reception will be held in our Creativity Center, located on 6.

Contemporary Arts Center, 44 E 6th St, Cincinnati, Cincinnati, Ohio 45202

Delta-Swamp blues guitarist Tab Benoit has announced a new run of dates for his “ Soul of the Swamp ” tour. The additional shows include a stop in Cincinnati, OH at Taft Theatre on Friday, October 9 and will include support from The Ghalia Volt Band.

About TAB BENOIT

Tab Benoit is a four-time Grammy-nominated singer, songwriter and guitarist who, for more than thirty years, has built a remarkable career on the foundation of his gritty and soulful Delta swamp blues. He has acquired a devoted legion of fans along the way, as well as five Blues Music Awards, including BB King Entertainer of the Year (twice) and an induction into The Louisiana Music Hall of Fame.

The Creative Writing Project: Fall

42Contemporary Arts Center

museum

Details

The Creative Writing Project is a series of workshops designed to provide adult writers of all levels with opportunities to explore the art of creative writing. Each month-long series puts participants amongst a community of writers and educators, offering instruction and guidance from a diverse group of local and published writers. Throughout the series, writers will explore methods such as poetry, nonfiction, and prose.

The October sessions will tie in with the upcoming FotoFocus and CAC exhibition, In the Interest of Time, with time being the main theme of the writing series.

Series Costs (4 sessions): This program is sold together as a 4 session series. $110 for Non-Members, $85 for CAC Members or students.

27Aronoff Center for the Arts · Jarson-Kaplan Theater

Free · film · indigenous peoples day

Details

Presented in partnership with the Cincinnati Arts Association and the Aronoff Center Jarson-Kaplan Theater, Urban Native Collective's Artist and Speaker Series brings contemporary artists to highlight that Indigenous expression is not a recovery of what was lost, but an explosive celebration of what has always survived. Moving beyond colonial narratives, the gathering honors Indigenous life as a living, Sovereign, and evolving force. Grounded in an "Indigenized" punk aesthetic, this multidisciplinary showcase demonstrates that Indigenous presence, creative defiance, and joy are the ultimate forces shaping our shared future.

MoreWorkshop

Multisensory Gallery Discussion: Sensing Change

38Cincinnati Art Museum

museum · adults general · art making experiences

Details

This inclusive program will be a multisensorial gallery discussion followed by an art making experience that features connections between sight, sound, smell, touch and sometimes taste. Facilitation of this program is provided by a new partnership with Art Equals. This organization fosters community-driven, accessible opportunities for creative growth and healing. At each program, visitors will encounter a few select works of art and explore each one using multiple senses. Facilitators will introduce the artwork through detailed description, music, movement, smells, and tactiles. After exploring these works of art in the galleries, the facilitator will lead the group to the classroom for a tactile, all-ability art-making experience related to the day's gallery.

Cost: Registration required. $5 for general public Free for members
